thread:
kai: Kicking off EU7 cloud account + VNet delivery for the new GPU cluster. Need short checklist sign-off: CIDR, cross-account peering, quota requests (GPUs + ENIs), Terraform module version, and cost center tagging. @amanda @jeff can you review?

amanda: Quick check — what CIDR range are we proposing? We need to avoid overlap with customer-managed networks in eu-west3.

jeff: Proposal from infra planning was 10.80.0.0/16 for shared services, 10.81.0.0/16 for gpu-prod, 10.82.0.0/16 for gpu-stage. Keeps /16s per pool for future subnets. Any objections?

natalie: Fine by networking. Make sure we add a /28 for peering endpoints and keep the AZ subnet mapping doc updated. I can update the spreadsheet after we lock it.

kai: Sounds good. Two immediate action items: 1) submit quota request for 100 A100s (start lower if asked) + 500 ENIs, 2) create account in org with tags: dept=infra, project=eu7-gpu, cost_center=ML(042). I'll draft the terraform scaffold.

jeff: For quota request, ops-bot has an internal template. Use this snippet for the support body:

```
Region: eu7
Request: Increase GPU quota
Instance family: A100-80GB
Desired: 100
Use case: Redwood inference dedicated cluster bring-up
Contact: infra-oncall@redwood.com
```

amanda: Also need IAM roles: compute-admin limited to machine create, networking-admin for VPC peering, and a read-only billing role tied to cost_center. We should use roles from `roles/infra-template` so handoffs are consistent.

infra-oncall: Note from oncall: ensure we request quota per AZ if provider requires it. Also request burst quota for initial scale tests and include expected steady-state utilization to avoid throttling.

sre-bot: FYI — previous eu region had a peering MTU issue. Add validation step to exercise jumbo frames on path between GPU cluster subnet and storage subnet.

kai: Good catch. I'll add a validation step in the runbook: ping/iperf between a GPU node and a storage node, check MTU and packet loss. Also add flow logs + VPC reachability analyzer run.

natalie: Terraform notes — use module `redwood/vpc/aws` v2.4.1, enable `flow_logs = true`, and set `enable_dns_hostnames = true`. Example resource block:

```
module "eu7_vpc" {
  source = "git::ssh://git@repo/redwood/terraform//modules/vpc?ref=v2.4.1"
  cidr_block = "10.80.0.0/16"
  enable_flow_logs = true
  tags = { Name = "eu7-shared" dept = "infra" project = "eu7-gpu" }
}
```

jeff: Also ensure the subnet AZ mapping table uses provider AZ names, not logical names. We've had drift there before.

kai: Action summary:
- kai: open cloud account skeleton and push terraform scaffold
- amanda: finalize CIDR map and IAM role list
- jeff: submit quota request using ops-bot template
- natalie: update AZ mapping doc and subnet spreadsheet
- infra-oncall: run early validation once we have 1 GPU node up

jeff: Submitted quota ticket 7891011 with the support team. ETA 48-72h. :thumbsup:

ops-bot: Support ticket 7891011 status: PENDING. Assigned to cloud-quotas@provider.com

sre-bot: Quota approved for 50 A100s initially, with staged approval to 100 after verification. Ticket 7891011 CLOSED -> 7891011-A

amanda: Ok I'll shrink initial plan to 50 GPUs for the first rollout and include a canary lane with 4 nodes.

kai: Perfect. Once quota confirmed and terraform applied, we'll run the validation checklist: subnets, route tables, peering, security groups (least-priv), MTU test, flow logs verification, and cost tag validation. After that we'll do a handoff doc for oncall + SRE.

natalie: Minor note — set a billing alert in provider console for project=eu7-gpu at $8k/month to catch unexpected spend during warm-up.

kai: Thanks all. I'll create the handoff thread when validations pass and attach the runbook. Closing this thread once the first apply succeeds. :white_check_mark:
